build_note: Installed from the pinned pure-Python py3-none-any wheel by hash; the image checks that the wheel's dirtyjson/ package is byte-identical to the pinned sdist and that dirtyjson/loader.py, __init__.py, attributed_containers.py, LICENSE.txt and the bundled simplejson.LICENSE.txt match recorded SHA-256 values. No runtime dependencies.
dependencies_note: atheris 3.1.0 is the in-process fuzz bridge only; dirtyjson has no runtime dependencies.
parser_family: dirtyjson pure-Python lenient decoder (dirtyjson/loader.py DirtyJSONLoader), described by its README as a fairly drastically rewritten version of the simplejson loader and shipping simplejson's license: simplejson-derived lineage, shared with the selected simplejson path, not byte-shared code; it neither imports nor delegates to the standard json module
api: dirtyjson.loads(local JSON bytes); dirtyjson.loads(decoded str) and dirtyjson.load(local binary stream) are checked against the same oracle
coverage: Python line tracing of dirtyjson package source (loader.py, attributed_containers.py and helpers) during valid-control replay; Atheris import instrumentation for the byte-input bridge
scope: JSON structure and values from local bytes via dirtyjson.loads; valid nested object and nested array controls only, each matching an exact type-tagged CPython json oracle tree. dirtyjson is a lenient decoder: it accepts comments, unquoted keys, single quotes and trailing commas and returns AttributedDict/AttributedList (dict/list subclasses carrying source positions), so it does not reject non-RFC 8259 input.
